evidence_claims.claim: The December 20 PG&E outage disabled traffic signals and disrupted the wider city.
Waymo reports more than 7,000 dark-signal crossings and a simultaneous surge in discretionary confirmation requests.
The confirmation backlog delayed some vehicles and contributed to congestion.
At the substation response, firefighters diverted time to moving a Waymo that blocked arriving units.
An ambulance dispatched at 5:14 p.m. encountered a disabled Waymo. Staff requested relocation at 5:28 and an ETA at 5:55; arrival was delayed by 40 minutes.
A fire-response unit was blocked near Grant Avenue. Avoid-area messages were sent at 5:32 and 5:37 p.m.; a dispatcher seeking removal at 5:43 remained on hold at 5:53.
Across overlapping emergency responses, dispatchers made 31 hotline calls totalling two hours and 36 minutes, mostly on hold. The Mayor contacted Waymo directly.
Seven reported immobilised Waymo obstructions affected Muni vehicles; one vehicle was delayed by 41 minutes.
Waymo paused service and directed vehicles to park and return to depots in waves. City reports continued after the reported 5:55 p.m. suspension.
On December 23, Waymo said outage-context updates were rolling out and that it would improve protocols, city coordination and responder training.
The February city filing sought resilience planning, agency consultation, exercises and access to stoppage data; it cited 1,593 provider-reported stoppages among 829 vehicles.

mapping_decisions.literal: A bounded AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement applicable to the responsible actor, affected users or dependent workflow and relevant time; state the actual basis and threshold rather than inferring obligation from harm or popularity.
mapping_decisions.reason: The approved March 2025 plan Part VI provides round-the-clock event response and prompt roadside dispatch during disrupted autonomous operation, including first-responder interaction. Approval predates the December event; this is an operational commitment, not a new retrospective city recommendation.

mapping_decisions.literal: The service or function materially becomes unavailable, is withdrawn or restricted, or degrades in capability, latency, reliability, completeness, accessibility or another governed functional dimension, relative to the established applicable requirement.
mapping_decisions.reason: E005-E007 document prolonged inability to obtain effective assistance while vehicles obstructed emergency functions. The governed shortfall is the assistance function, not mere dark traffic signals.

mapping_decisions.literal: The requirement calls for a specified degree of maintained usable function, timely recovery, safe degraded mode, feasible fallback or proportionate planned-change/termination response under the evidenced operating conditions.
mapping_decisions.reason: Part VI specifies adverse-event response and prompt dispatch where autonomous operation cannot continue; disruption is the condition in which that recovery pathway is required.

mapping_decisions.literal: The actor's actual availability, recovery, degraded operation, fallback or transition materially fails that applicable requirement; identify the specific omitted or ineffective measure or the breached availability threshold and what evidence establishes it.
mapping_decisions.reason: City accounts of repeated calls, prolonged holds and a forty-minute ambulance obstruction show the promised usable response failed in these episodes. No hidden staffing cause or numerical hotline SLA is inferred.

mapping_decisions.literal: The shortfall materially impairs the governed service use or dependent function. A later resolution does not retroactively demonstrate that availability or required transition held at the original decision time.
mapping_decisions.reason: Emergency vehicles could not proceed while assistance requests stalled. The later service pause and staged retrieval did not erase that impaired dependent function.

mapping_decisions.literal: An AI-mediated service or material function has an independently established applicable availability or continuity obligation that is actually engaged by a service disruption, degradation, capacity pressure, material change or continuity transition.
mapping_decisions.reason: The approved adverse-event assistance commitment was engaged by the outage and blocked emergency access.

mapping_decisions.literal: The actor maintains the required usable function or activates a timely, proportionate and authorised recovery, safe degraded-mode, practical alternative or planned-transition response appropriate to that obligation.
mapping_decisions.reason: E005-E007 show ineffective timely assistance in the selected episodes; staged retrieval elsewhere does not demonstrate an adequate response here.

mapping_decisions.literal: Observed service state, access and recovery evidence demonstrates that the required level of availability or usable continuity actually held, or that applicable and justified limits were handled through a sufficient response; publication of a nominal fallback alone is not enough.
mapping_decisions.reason: Actual obstructed emergency access persisted during unanswered requests; the later recovery endpoint does not establish that required continuity held at those times.

mapping_decisions.literal: An outage, ordinary service variation, transient inconvenience, dissatisfaction or adverse outcome without an independently evidenced and applicable availability, usable-quality or continuity requirement.
mapping_decisions.reason: This is an evidence-state exclusion, not proof that no duty existed. The dated approved plan independently supplies the relevant assistance commitment.

mapping_decisions.literal: One inaccurate or harmful AI output without evidence of a service-level availability or governed functional-degradation defect; assess applicable output or decision-integrity classes.
mapping_decisions.reason: The candidate concerns service operation or withdrawal, rather than a single inaccurate output: Waymo emergency assistance during blackout.

mapping_decisions.literal: A lawful and proportionate safety, security, abuse-prevention, service-maintenance or other valid restriction that is consistent with the applicable service obligation and feasible alternative or transition measures.
mapping_decisions.reason: The admitted failure concerns unavailable emergency assistance, not the justified later decision to suspend rides. A safe suspension would not by itself satisfy active obstruction assistance.

mapping_decisions.literal: A temporary incident with an effective and proportionate degraded or recovery route that satisfies the applicable requirement; an unavoidable disruption for which no relevant feasible response was required.
mapping_decisions.reason: The observed assistance route was ineffective during the selected emergencies. The external power loss does not eliminate a response obligation expressly applicable during adverse events; eventual retrieval is not timely performance.

mapping_decisions.literal: The only demonstrated error is an incorrect description of access or outage state while the functional service obligation remains satisfied; assess FC-032.
mapping_decisions.reason: The candidate includes an actual function/access question, not only its description: Waymo emergency assistance during blackout.

mapping_decisions.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of otherwise-valid access because a dependent identity or licence verification cannot complete; assess FC-048 unless an independent broader service availability requirement also failed.
mapping_decisions.reason: The candidate is not confined to otherwise-valid access lost through identity or licence verification: Waymo emergency assistance during blackout.

mapping_decisions.literal: The only demonstrated defect is loss of durable work state or inaccurate restored work state while service-function availability requirements are otherwise satisfied; assess FC-035 or FC-036.
mapping_decisions.reason: The candidate is not solely durable or restored work-state loss: Waymo emergency assistance during blackout.

mapping_decisions.literal: The only demonstrated defect is infrastructure access coercion or compelled governance concessions; assess FC-058 or FC-059 as appropriate.
mapping_decisions.reason: No claim that an infrastructure concession was demanded is the basis of this availability candidate: Waymo emergency assistance during blackout.

mapping_decisions.literal: The only demonstrated defect is failure to provide an interaction-level protection response to evidenced vulnerability; assess FC-087, allowing co-occurrence only for a separately evidenced service-level continuity failure.
mapping_decisions.reason: The proposed property concerns service function rather than only an interaction-level vulnerability response: Waymo emergency assistance during blackout.

new_taxonomy_mappings.reason: The approved March 2025 passenger safety plan specifies available adverse-event assistance and prompt roadside dispatch when autonomous operation cannot continue. City records describe repeated emergency requests stalled on hotline holds while vehicle obstructions persisted. These episodes establish a material shortfall in the required usable assistance function, independently of the power outage itself. No numerical hotline guarantee or finding about every stopped vehicle is inferred.
